gate_outcome_note: Pending. Appended after the parent gate closes this stage.
material_selection_reason: Resolved by scripts/resolve-opencode-worker.mjs with no delegation-lifecycle violations. The stage qualifies on Recoverability and Economy. Recoverability is the substantive one: the repair applies page.clock.install()/fastForward, a pattern with zero precedent anywhere in this repository, to assertions owned by three other milestones, and it must be iterated against real Playwright runs. Running that iteration in a disposable worktree keeps the orchestrator's context unaffected if it goes wrong and lets the stage be re-run from clean. Economy is real: the qualified route is currently free. Among two eligible candidates showing no material stage-specific evidence advantage over one another, the active availability_economic temporary preference of 2026-08-21 selects ox-alpha; its free route was confirmed live at preflight and it closed this slice's stage 1 the same day at a PASS gate with no constraint breach. No concrete native material advantage applies. Direct execution was considered and rejected on its merits, NOT on accumulated context: see delegation_evaluation_note.

native-subagent: not filtered on capability; it lost the comparison. The stage is meaningful bounded implementation with a precise plan, an objective gate, and a disposable worktree, which is squarely inside the external candidate's qualified scope. It needs no native-only tooling and no MCP operation.

delegation_evaluation_note: The parent holds context on all three target files from gate-reviewing the delegated stage-1 return, which the workflow requires it to do. That context is recorded here explicitly and was NOT used as a direct-execution reason. 'The orchestrator already has context' is the named anti-pattern, and here it would be coupling the parent manufactured by reviewing rather than a property of the stage. No stage-2 target-file discovery was performed before this decision: nothing was read to work out how to rewrite an assertion.
consequence_basis: Three test assertions, each independently revertible as its own commit, behind an independent-verification gate whose explicit substance is reproducing the stochastic claim. Below the candidate's medium ceiling. The failure mode that matters is not a crash but a test that goes green without proving what it did, which is why the constraint is written as a hard boundary in the packet and why the parent diffs every hunk.

preflight_findings.write_isolation: SATISFIED. Disposable worktree D:/Projects/fitway-worktrees/p11-browser-debt-w01 prepared per docs/WORKFLOW.md steps 7-8: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile exit 0 in 13.2s, then the gate pnpm exec vitest --version returned vitest/4.1.10 win32-x64 node-v24.14.0.
preflight_findings.playwright_drive_and_read_failure_output: SATISFIED. pnpm exec playwright test tests/browser/phase3.browser.spec.ts in that worktree ran 3 tests, 3 passed in 16.5s, with the vite dev webServer started by the Playwright config.
preflight_findings.secret_provisioning: NOT REQUIRED, and this is the finding that changed the routing. The assumption going in was that a browser run needs .env and that provisioning real secrets into an external worker's worktree would be the blocker, since dotenv_contents is an excluded payload class. The probe refutes it: the three target specs mock every route and need no .env at all. The excluded payload class never enters the packet and the worker is never given a secret.
preflight_findings.verify_full_split: The worker does NOT run pnpm verify:full. That step needs a disposable Postgres database and .env, so the orchestrator runs it twice at the candidate. The approved plan pre-authorized this split as acceptable provided it is recorded. It is recorded here.
